newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS -Baht hit by dollar,devaluation talk.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS -Baht hit by dollar,devaluation talk.

text.p: * Thai baht remains under pressure from bullish dollar/majors. Central bank denial of devaluation rumour calms market but has little impact on exchange rate.
* Malaysian ringgit bounces back on trade minister's comment, but remains below 2.48 to the dollar.
* Indonesian rupiah slips amid ample liquidity, which pushes short-term swaps down.
* Singapore dollar falls through 1.41 support on U.S. dollar's continued rally.
The Thai baht remained under pressure from a surging dollar/yen on Thursday with the market showing little reaction to the central bank's denial of early devaluation rumours.

"The denial has tentatively slowed the (dollar's) rise and calmed the market a little. But unless dollar/yen corrects downwards, the dollar/baht is not likely to come back off," said Alison Seng, technical analyst at MMS International.

The baht was quoted at 25.820-25.830 to the dollar at 0430 GMT against 25.798-25.808 late on Wednesday. It briefly recovered to 25.814-25.819 after the Bank of Thailand (BOT) denied the devaluation rumours, started in offshore markets.

"We wish to categorically deny some rumours in the market that the baht may be devalued. The baht is only weak against the the U.S. dollar because the dollar is now very strong," a senior BOT official told Reuters.
"The rumours in the market are unfounded. The central bank is closely monitoring the baht now," the BOT official said.

Dealers said the dollar was likely to continue trading well above the central bank's dollar/baht mid-rate, fixed at 25.79 on Thursday, the lowest level since August 20, 1991 when the mid-rate was at 25.82.
"I reckon dollar/baht shouldn't go above 25.85. But for today it should linger around 25.80-25.84," said a senior dealer with a Thai bank in Singapore.
He said the central bank's recommendation that commercial banks hedge their currency risks in the light of the dollar's recent bull run had caused some confusion among banks.

"Some banks took it as the central bank losing its grip on the currency," he said, adding that rumours the BOT had advised banks and corporations to unwind their basket positions also added to the devaluation talk.

In Malaysia, the ringgit bounced back briefly but remained within its recent range following comments by the trade and industry minister, who said the currency's rise against the dollar this month would not affect foreign investment inflows.
"Dollar/ringgit was at 2.4860/70. It came down to about 2.4820 after the comment," said a Japanese bank dealer in Singapore.
"It should be supported at 2.4800, but the topside may be limited because people will use this (the comment) as an excuse to sell on rallies," he added.
Research firm I.D.E.A. said in a daily comment that the trade minister's statement reinforced the perception that "the government does not view a strong ringgit with any degree of alarm."
"The bias of pressure on the ringgit is now turning more bullish with a rise above 2.4800 expected in the coming sessions," it said.
Kuala Lumpur dealers said the ringgit could undergo a short-term correction but it was likely to remain in favour.
"Once the correction is over, funds will come back to the Malay (currency) because they want to establish positive yield positions," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.

Rumours of a trade deficit for November 1996 were also capping the ringgit's gains, dealers said. In a poll by Reuters on Tuesday, economists from 10 research houses forecast an average deficit of 148 million ringgit for November.
The figures are widely expected to be released on Friday.
Further south, the Singapore dollar finally broke through the 1.41 level in the face of the U.S. dollar's almost relentless rise against the mark and yen.
"Dollar/Sing is still lagging behind the dollar/majors," said the Thai bank dealer.
He said there were some U.S. dollar sell orders around the S$1.4100 level, but these were unlikely to pose a strong barrier as players were very bullish on the U.S. unit.
The Indonesian rupiah slipped amid ample liquidity, which pulled down short-term swaps and drove interest rates in the money market to follow suit.
"The market this morning is mainly liquidity-driven. There seems to be some fresh government transfers for civil servants' 13th month salaries," said a local bank dealer in Jakarta.
The payment was linked to the upcoming Eid al-Fitr celebration on February 9 and 10.
Dealers said sentiment on the dollar appeared to be bullish at present, prompting some operators to go long on dollars.
The local bank dealer said the declining swaps trend might encourage some players to go long as the dollar's downside was limited by the central bank intervention band.
He added, however, that the central bank's fixing policy needed to be monitored as it had depreciated the rupiah by only one point so far against four points last week.
Spot rupiah was at 2,373.00/74.00 at 0430 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,371.25/71.75.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (62-21-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
